answer: Each identity must grow its claim as a cedar on its own ledge: a narrow shelf of rock that holds one tree and no more, built only from its verified jobs of this epoch. The cedar grows one ring per epoch, each ring a single verified job, and an opal set into the trunk counts only when three independent peers, looking from three different angles, see the same fire in it. A cedar whose rings do not reach this epoch, or an opal that flashes a borrowed color, is felled from the ledge on the spot. Ten voices need ten cedars and ten separate ledges, because no ring can be lent to a clone.
